title: Surrey Home Energy Rebates 2026: Heat Pumps, Insulation and Solar
desc: Surrey rebates for 2026 from BC Hydro, FortisBC and CleanBC, built around Surrey's 185,670 households, the largest count after Vancouver.
badge: Heat pumps up to $4,000, insulation up to $5,500
lead: Surrey has 185,670 households, more than any BC city except Vancouver, and the youngest housing stock in this group: only 20% of homes were built before 1981.
cards_heading: What you can claim in Surrey in 2026
cards_intro: Amounts come from the program pages we re-read on October 2, 2026. Each card is a maximum, and most depend on how your home is heated.

cards.title: Whole-home heat pump
cards.note: Must replace electric heat such as baseboards or an electric furnace, meet 100% of the heating load at -5C and be installed by a Home Performance Contractor Network member.

cards.title: Partial heat pump
cards.note: For a heat pump that covers at least half of the heating load while replacing electric heat.

cards.title: Limited-time bonus
cards.note: Extra money on heat pump installs completed between August 1 and October 31, 2026.

cards.title: Community top-ups (select postal codes)
cards.note: Only select postal codes in Campbell Heights. Heat pump top-up, plus $1,750 more on a Level 2 EV charger and double appliance rebates.

cards.title: Income-qualified switch from gas, oil or propane
cards.note: CleanBC pays by income level (Level 3 / Level 2 / Level 1) for a central or three-head heat pump, for invoices from July 6, 2026.

cards.title: Insulation
cards.note: Attic, wall and basement or crawlspace work, paid per R-value added per square foot. Homes heated mainly by electricity only.

cards.title: Windows and doors
cards.note: $100 per opening, with a U-factor of 1.22 or lower.

cards.title: Heat pump water heater
cards.note: Only when it replaces an electric water heater.

cards.title: Solar panels
cards.note: $1,000 per kW, capped at half the cost, from an HPCN member installer.

cards.title: Battery storage
cards.note: Up to $1,500 on its own with solar, or up to $5,000 with Peak Saver enrolment.

cards.title: EV charger
cards.note: 50% of a new wall-mounted Level 2 charger, plus $200 for a power-management device.

sections: The 2021 Census counted 185,670 households in Surrey. Of these, 70% own and about 33% live in detached houses. Only 20% live in homes built before 1981, but because the city is so large that is still 12,485 owner-occupied detached houses, the biggest pool among the cities we track outside Vancouver. Major repairs were reported by 3.8% of households, the lowest share in the set.

BC Hydro's community-based offers reach only one part of Surrey: select postal codes in Campbell Heights. If you live there, a heat pump that replaces electric heat earns $4,000 more (whole home) or $1,500 more (partial). In the same postal codes, a Level 2 EV charger at a single-family home gets a $1,750 top-up (up to the full cost) on top of the $350 rebate, if you apply between August 4 and December 31, 2026 and enroll the charger in Peak Saver for its $250 bonus. And select ENERGY STAR fridges, washers and dryers get double the regular rebate (see our BC appliance rebates page). Everywhere else in Surrey, the amounts in the cards above are what you can expect. Check your address on BC Hydro's postal code checker.
How that changes which rebate comes first

Because most Surrey homes are newer, the attic and wall insulation rebate matters less on average than it does in Kamloops or Victoria. The sized heat pump and heat pump water heater are the more common first projects for an electric-heated home. A pre-1981 Surrey house, meanwhile, is a strong candidate for all three: BC Hydro pays up to $5,500 for insulation, up to $4,000 for a heat pump and up to $2,000 for windows, within an overall ceiling that BC Hydro lists at $12,500.

Surrey electricity is BC Hydro. If your home heats with natural gas, the gas utility is FortisBC, and BC Hydro will not rebate a heat pump that replaces gas. Income-qualified households can get $3,500, $7,000 or $13,000 from CleanBC. Everyone else should look at insulation and a heat pump water heater, and compare financing, since we found no standard provincial rebate above the income limits.
The January average low is 0.7°C and the record in 2015 to 2024 was -16.7°C. Solar gets about 3.38 peak sun hours a day. A cold-climate heat pump handles that range easily.

claim_steps: Check your heating fuel on a recent bill.
If you are electric, price a heat pump with an HPCN installer.
If you are on gas, check the CleanBC income limits.
Ask about insulation if the house is from before 1981.
Keep invoices and apply within six months.
faq: Is Surrey's housing older or newer than Burnaby's?
Newer. Surrey has 20% of households in pre-1981 homes against 35% in Burnaby.
How many older owner-occupied houses does Surrey have?
The 2021 Census counts 12,485 owner-occupied detached houses built before 1981.
The BC Hydro account holder applies or signs a consent form. Renters make up about 30% of households.
What is the maximum I can collect?
BC Hydro lists up to $12,500 in total for multiple upgrades, including a bonus of up to $2,000.
